みち に まよったら — If you get lost
You say “if” with ～ば (a condition) and “when / whenever” with ～と (an automatic result), give directions and ask “what should I do?”: どう すれば いい です か.
If you walk fast, you’ll make it in time.
If you go straight along this street, you’ll come out in a square.
When spring comes, the cherry trees blossom.
I should have brought the map.
To form ～ば: いく → いけば, たべる → たべれば, たかい → たかければ, しずか → しずか なら.
To use ～と for certain, automatic results: ボタン を おす と、ドア が あきます.
To give directions with ～と: まっすぐ いく と、みぎ に…
To ask for advice: どう すれば いい です か.
To express regret: ～ば よかった.
Monday morning, at Madrid airport. Haruka and Sakura have landed. Ana has come to pick them up. Kenji knows nothing.
Sakura, how big you’ve grown! Haruka, it was a long flight, you must be tired.
Thank you. Does Kenji really know nothing?
He knows nothing. When he opens the restaurant at twelve, he always tastes the broth on his own. If we go then, he’ll definitely be amazed.
About thirty minutes by metro. If we leave now, we’ll be there in time.
Then let’s hurry. Sakura, take your bag.
Ana, if I get lost, what should I do?
Don’t get lost! But if it happens, show this card. The restaurant’s address is written on it.
I see. And besides, if I smell Daddy’s ramen, I’ll know straight away!
(Laughing) This girl has a very good nose.
“ba” short and clear at the end: i-ke-ba, ta-be-re-ba, ta-ka-ke-re-ba. Don’t drag out the vowel.
mas-su-gu: the double pause (っ) before す.
shin-goh: the “n” is a whole syllable, the “o” is long.
いい → よければ (not “いければ”). Just like いい → よかった.
You’ve already seen the form なければ in ～なければ なりません (must). Now you know where it comes from: “if you don’t, it won’t do”.
～ば stresses the CONDITION: “if (and only if) X, then Y”.
If we leave now, we’ll make it in time.
What should I do? (If I do it how, is it good?)
I should have brought the map. (a regret)
After ～ば, you usually DON’T put a request or an invitation (～て ください, ～ましょう) when the first verb is an action. Use ～たら there: ついたら でんわ して ください.
Dictionary form + と = “when / whenever X, Y (definitely) happens”. It’s for laws of nature, habits, machines and DIRECTIONS:
If you press this button, the door opens.
If you go straight on, the station is on the right.
After ～と you CAN’T put your own will (～たい, ～ましょう, ～て ください). “When you get home, call me” = ついたら でんわ して ください (not つく と).
4. Review: たら, ば, と, なら
all-purpose; “after / when / if”; works with requests
picks up the other person’s topic; advice before an action
If you don’t know which to choose, use ～たら: it’s the most flexible and rarely wrong.
“If you go straight on, the station is on the right.”
If you turn left, there’s the bank.

ケンジ の みせ への ちず — The way to Kenji’s restaurant
The directions Ana wrote on Sakura’s card.
From the Puerta del Sol, use the bear statue as a landmark.
From in front of the bear statue, if you go straight along the big street, you come to a traffic light.
Cross at the traffic light, turn left and you come out in a little street.
At the third corner of the little street there’s a red lantern. That’s the restaurant.
If you don’t know, show someone this card.
What is the landmark in the Puerta del Sol?
Which way do you turn after the traffic light?
How do you recognise the restaurant?
あかい ちょうちん を さがして — Looking for the red lantern
At twelve sharp, Kenji opened the restaurant door as usual.
Then he went back to the kitchen and tasted a spoonful of broth.
At that moment a voice came from behind him.
“What a lovely smell. You can smell it all the way to Hiroshima.”
Kenji turned round. And dropped the ladle.
Haruka was standing at the door.
“Haruka… how… weren’t you supposed to come next week…”
“We wanted to come early and surprise you. Ana helped us.”
Kenji couldn’t say anything. His eyes had gone red.
Haruka and Ana looked at each other. Then they turned to look behind them.
When they got off the metro, they had definitely been together. In the Puerta del Sol, Sakura had been taking photos of the bear statue.
“That was it,” said Ana. “There were lots of people and we went on ahead.”
Haruka went pale. “What do I do? What should I do…”
Meanwhile, Sakura was standing alone in the Puerta del Sol.
After taking the photo, she turned round and neither her mother nor Ana was there.
All around were strangers. Everyone was speaking Spanish.
Sakura’s eyes filled with tears. But she thought she mustn’t cry.
“If I cry, I won’t be able to see anything. If I think, I’ll work it out.”
Sakura took the card out of her pocket. The card Ana had written for her.
“From the bear statue, if you go straight along the big street, you come to a traffic light.”
The bear statue was right there. But there were lots of big streets. Which one could it be?
Sakura closed her eyes and sniffed the air.
The smell of churros. The smell of cars. The smell of flowers. And, very faintly…
When she walked in the direction of the smell, she came to a traffic light. Just like on the card.
She crossed, turned left and came out in a little street.
But there she got confused. There were lots of corners and she didn’t know which was the third.
Sakura plucked up her courage and showed the card to the old lady at the bakery.
“Ra… ramen. Daddy.” She knew very few words of Spanish.
But as soon as the old lady read the card, she smiled broadly: “Ah, Kenji!”
Kenji was famous on that street. He bought bread at this bakery every morning.
The old lady took Sakura by the hand and walked her to the third corner.
The red lantern came into view.
Just then, Kenji rushed out of the restaurant. Behind him were Haruka and Ana.
Sakura ran and threw herself into Kenji’s arms. And only then did she cry. She cried a lot.
That evening, the restaurant was closed for a private party. In the place of honour sat the old lady from the bakery.
Kenji made the old lady his very best ramen. She ate ramen for the first time and said: “Delicious!”
Eating her ramen, Sakura said quietly: “I thought that if I looked at the card I’d know. But if I didn’t have this nose, I wouldn’t have found the way.”
Haruka laughed. But her eyes were still a little red.
“From now on, all you have to do is not let go of my hand.”
Kenji put his arms round both of them and said quietly: “I don’t need any map. If my family is here, anywhere is home.”
Late that night, Ana went home and told Mihai everything.
“If I’d been more careful, Sakura wouldn’t have got lost.”
Mihai put his hand on Ana’s shoulder: “But if you hadn’t written her that card, Sakura couldn’t have got to the restaurant.”
Ana thought for a moment and smiled: “That’s true. And lucky she has such a good nose.”
